site.name: Crow No. 36
site.location: Nederland / Boulder County Tungsten Mining District
overview: Crow No. 36 is a documented historic tungsten mine in the Nederland-area Boulder County tungsten district.

Colorado Geological Survey records place the named working in Section 12, Township 1 South, Range 73 West, across Colorado 119 and the gulch east of Mud Lake, and document a shaft with underground drifts.

timeline.text: Crow No. 36 was developed as an underground tungsten mine in the Nederland-area district and became one of the district's more productive small mines.
Colorado's tungsten-mine inventory recorded a 50-foot shaft, drifts on a network of small veins, and unusually high-grade ferberite concentrate from the property.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey MI-04 places Crow No. 36 across Colorado 119 and the gulch east of Mud Lake. It reports production of less than 10,000 tungsten units, a 50-foot shaft with drifts, and coarse crystalline ferberite concentrate reported at 70 to 74 percent.
The mine remains a named feature on Nederland-area U.S. Geological Survey topographic mapping, providing an independent geographic cross-check for the historic working.

For identification, the USGS/GNIS-derived named mine locality at approximately 39.9627648, -105.5099978 is used together with the Colorado Geological Survey's bounded location description. The point is a historic mine-level anchor, not a claim that a surviving shaft collar has been field surveyed or is safe to approach.
